inhalt.name: Virtuv
inhalt.zweck: Terminal: plan every project as a flow first, approve it, then build it in the same terminal.
inhalt.zielgruppe: Claude Code users who want to plan before building.

anforderungen.text: Flow appears in browser 10 seconds after the idea.
New version opens in browser by itself.
Blocks: max 4 words.
Changes since last version highlighted in color.
Comments survive a reload.
Add, move, delete blocks and draw arrows by mouse.
Approve locked while a comment or question is open.
Claude receives all comments and changes.
Approved version cannot be changed.
Claude receives the URS only after approval.
One sentence per requirement, no source or extra fields.
A new block never covers an existing one.
Shift+Enter: new line in terminal and block field, without sending.
Folder column shown/hidden by click.
Side panel shown/hidden by click.
Before approval: plan only, no building.
After approval: build only the approved version, in the same terminal.
New wish while building: back to planning.
Window header shows: Planning or Building.
Hidden columns stay hidden after restart.
Terminal shown/hidden by click.
Column widths draggable by mouse.
Column widths kept after restart.
Claude ticks off addressed comments itself.
Claude uses the user's own Claude Code settings and tools.
Remove project from overview without deleting files.
Ctrl+T opens a new chat without closing the others.
Side panel: button to collapse, strip to expand.
Clicking a block opens the side panel.
Block field: input and button only, no hint texts.
Unapproved blocks and requirements carry a “new” tag.
Chat name = project name, no extra line.
Double-click renames chat permanently.
New chat always asks for a folder.
Ctrl+W closes the current chat.
Folder names with leading/trailing spaces can be opened.
URS of a subfolder can be planned in the same chat.
Claude sees the flowchart as an image after every draft.
Screenshots insertable via Cmd+V or drag; Claude sees them.
Blocks, arrows, labels never overlap.
Flowchart arranges itself top to bottom.
U numbers only in side panel, not on blocks.
Claude fixes overlaps before the user sees the version.
Blocks moved by hand stay in place.
“Tidy up” button rearranges the flowchart.
Version number top left next to app name.
Every new build: higher version number.
Each requirement: max 12 words.
Comparisons like “as in Warp” are forbidden.
Each requirement checked for SMART independently, not by its author.
Claude fixes SMART violations before the user sees the version.
Each requirement belongs to exactly one block.
Approval only by button, never by Claude.
SMART result per requirement visible in side panel.
Approve locked while a requirement fails SMART.
Claude fixes overlaps before the user sees them.
Default language English: interface, blocks, requirements.
Language switch toggles interface between English and German.
Chosen language kept after restart.
App name: Virtuv.
Every project follows: plan, code, review, test, commit.
Every code change reviewed by an independent reviewer, not its author.
Testing starts only after all review findings are fixed.
Before commit: each change tested against its approved requirement.
Failed test: back to coding, no commit.
Every passed change committed to git with a message.
Test result per change shown in terminal: pass or fail.
Commits go to a separate branch, never directly to main.
After each commit: push to GitHub if a GitHub remote exists.
Claude Code users install Virtuv with two plugin commands.
Plugin passes the official Claude plugin check without errors.
Command /virtuv:plan starts planning in the current folder.
Plugin users review, comment and approve the flow in the browser.
Plugin and app show the same blocks, comments and approval state.
Plugin lives in public GitHub repo plutunieer/virtuv-plugin.
Step-by-step guide tells the user how to submit to Anthropic.
New chat starts planning without choosing a folder.
Building starts only after a folder is chosen.
Plan made without folder moves into the folder chosen later.
Ctrl+Tab switches to the next chat.
Cmd+1–9 opens the chat at that tab position.
Plugin icon: violet tile, three flow blocks, center diamond with check.
Icon file .claude-plugin/icon.png: PNG, 1024×1024 px, under 2 MB.
At 32 px: three blocks and diamond at least 1 px apart.
Icon is in the public plugin repo before submission.
Desktop app shows the same new icon as the plugin.
Product Hunt tagline in English, at most 60 characters.
Product Hunt description in English, at most 500 characters.
First maker comment in English, at most 800 characters.
Launch listing names exactly three Product Hunt topics.
Every feature named in the launch kit exists in approved URS.
Launch thumbnail: PNG, 240×240 px, showing the Virtuv icon.
Four launch gallery images, PNG, 1270×760 px each.
Gallery images show real Virtuv app screens only.
All launch texts and images shown on one browser page.
Launch checklist names date, time and every link to enter.
Every link in the launch kit returns HTTP status 200.
Launch kit files saved in folder launch and committed.
Only the user posts on Product Hunt, never Claude.
Public GitHub repo plutunieer/virtuv contains only README and releases.
Release v0.5.2 offers Virtuv-0.5.2-arm64.dmg for download.
README gives numbered steps to open Virtuv past the Gatekeeper warning.
Download button on virtuv.dev opens the latest GitHub release.
Latest release offers downloads for Mac Apple chip, Mac Intel, Windows.
Intel Mac download installs and starts Virtuv on an Intel Mac.
Windows installer installs and starts Virtuv on 64-bit Windows 11.
On Windows, Virtuv starts the installed Claude Code in its terminal.
virtuv.dev shows three download buttons, each downloading its system's file.
README gives numbered steps to open Virtuv past Windows SmartScreen.

fragen.text: No Windows PC or Intel Mac here. Who can test those downloads before launch?

sicherheit: Other websites can neither embed nor remote-control the app.
The flowchart image shows only the flowchart, never the rest of the screen.
Claude never logs in or posts on Product Hunt.
App source code is never published; the private repo stays private.
nichtEnthalten: Own change list or version comparison
Controlling the screen or other apps
Merging into main without the user's explicit consent
Paid plans or license checks in the plugin
Virtuv submitting to Anthropic's directory by itself
Changing the icon after the first submission
Product Hunt listing, texts and images (user creates them)
